peer_identity.arc_label: The last poet — 5,000-year disembodied head, then poet component within Melmoth
peer_identity.honcho_notes: Merge: OCR kr→kl transposition. zaran-krleza is canonical (correct spelling, authoritative 4-record card).
peer_identity.rationale: zaran-klezra (vol15 single-record singleton) and zaran-krleza (4-record merged card spanning vol11–14) are the same poet entity. 'Klezra' is an OCR transposition of 'Krleza' (kr→kl metathesis, ratio 0.917). zaran-krleza is the authoritative merged card with correct spelling and four source records; zaran-klezra is a later extraction artifact with the transposed form.

appearances: description: Disembodied human head with long white hair and beard, suspended in cables and machinery inside his fortress. Only the head survives of his original body.; source_refs: ['290_The_Metabarons_11_p13', '291_The_Metabarons_11_p14']
important_actions: Survived 5,000 years as a preserved disembodied head by sacrificing the rest of his body to keep his soul alive (p13)
Greeted Steelhead as a long-awaited 'culmination' and refused forced entry to his fortress (p08–p09)
Devised the soul trial: ancient bow without arrows, must defeat octo-tiger without killing it (p10)
Proposed and accepted surgical fusion with Steelhead's body; endured without anesthetic (p14)
knowledge_boundaries: Cannot pursue physical love — lacks a body; substitutes verbal/spiritual love
Poetry still survives within his mind even without a body (p13)
relationships: target: Steelhead / Melmoth; nature: Agreed to surgical fusion of his surviving head with Steelhead's body; both prior egos dissolved to produce Melmoth; source_refs: ['291_The_Metabarons_11_p14', '292_The_Metabarons_11_p15']
traits: Extremely patient — waited 5,000 years for his 'culmination'
Values soul and inner worth over combat strength
Sacrificed his body to preserve his soul and keep poetry alive
Contrasts verbal/spiritual love with physical/carnal love
Frames emotion as something that must be opened into, not academically taught
Believed dead or extinct for approximately 5,000 years before Steelhead found him
voice_notes: States emotions cannot be taught directly (p13)
Frames entry requirements as a soul trial, not a strength test: 'I want to judge your soul' (p08–p09)
Philosophy of love: verbal and spiritual love over carnal — regrets lack of body but does not regret the sacrifice (p13)
witnessed_facts: Many seekers attempted to reach his fortress over 50 centuries; none succeeded before Steelhead (p08–p09)
Steelhead passed his soul trial by producing music rather than violence (p12)
